Job Summary

We are looking for an experienced Android AOSP Hardware Enablement Engineer to bring up and enable automotive hardware platforms for Android Open Source Project (AOSP) and Android Automotive OS (AAOS) builds. The engineer will be responsible for enabling the underlying hardware and software stack required to build, boot, and operate Android on an automotive SoC platform. This includes bootloader configuration, Linux kernel integration, device tree development, vendor BSP integration, hardware driver enablement, Android build configuration, and debugging of hardware‑related boot and runtime issues. The candidate will work closely with SoC vendors, hardware teams, BSP developers, kernel engineers, and Android framework teams to deliver a stable and functional Android infotainment platform.

Key Responsibilities

AOSP Build System and Platform Integration

  • Set up and maintain AOSP source code and development environments.
  • Configure and execute Android platform builds using Soong, Android.bp, Make, and related build tools.
  • Integrate vendor‑provided Android BSP packages into the AOSP source tree.
  • Configure product definitions, device configurations, board configurations, and vendor‑specific build components.
  • Develop and maintain device‑specific build configurations, including device/, vendor/, and relevant kernel integration components.
  • Configure product makefiles, product packages, build variants, and system/vendor partition requirements.
  • Resolve build failures, dependency issues, missing modules, and compilation errors.
  • Maintain build scripts and documentation for repeatable platform builds.

Bootloader and Platform Bring‑Up

  • Enable the Android boot process on new or existing automotive hardware platforms.
  • Work with bootloaders such as U‑Boot or vendor‑specific implementations based on the target SoC.
  • Configure boot arguments, boot targets, image loading, memory reservations, and device‑tree handoff.
  • Coordinate with SoC vendors to resolve platform‑specific boot and firmware issues.

Linux Kernel and Device Tree Enablement

  • Integrate and configure vendor Linux kernels compatible with the selected Android release.
  • Enable required kernel configurations and device drivers for the target hardware.
  • Develop, modify, and debug Device Tree Source (DTS/DTSI) files and overlays.
  • Configure hardware resources such as GPIOs, clocks, regulators, interrupts, IOMMU, DMA, and memory regions.
  • Integrate vendor kernel modules and troubleshoot module loading or dependency issues.

Hardware Driver and Peripheral Enablement

  • Enable and validate hardware peripherals required for automotive infotainment, including:
  • Display interfaces (MIPI DSI, eDP, LVDS, HDMI)
  • Touchscreen controllers and input devices
  • Audio codecs, I²S/TDM interfaces, amplifiers, and routing
  • USB host/device controllers, storage, and connectivity
  • Wi‑Fi, Bluetooth, GNSS, Ethernet
  • Camera interfaces and sensors (where applicable)
  • I²C, SPI, UART, GPIO, PCIe, and other SoC peripherals
  • Automotive CAN interfaces and transceivers (where supported)
  • Power‑management ICs, thermal sensors, watchdogs, suspend/resume functionality

Hardware Debugging and System Validation

  • Debug the complete boot flow from bootloader to Android launcher.
  • Analyze bootloader logs, kernel dmesg, Android Logcat, tombstones, and service startup logs.
  • Use ADB, fastboot, serial consoles, JTAG, and other hardware debugging tools.

Automotive Platform Integration

  • Enable and validate Android Automotive OS on reference boards and target hardware.
  • Work with automotive SoC platforms and vendor BSPs from Qualcomm, NXP, MediaTek, etc.
  • Coordinate with hardware design, BSP, firmware, Android framework, and application teams.
  • Support hardware variants, board revisions, and product‑specific configurations.
  • Assist with Android compatibility testing and platform validation requirements.
  • Integrate automotive features such as vehicle properties, audio, display, connectivity, and power‑state management.
  • Follow applicable automotive development, security, and software quality requirements.

Role Overview

Polus provides identity and contact data to enterprise clients through APIs and bulk delivery. This role detects and stops misuse of that data: credential sharing, reselling access, scraping, queries that fall outside a client's permitted purpose, and automated harvesting. You'll build the detection systems, not just monitor them. The work is behavioral analysis at scale: finding the few accounts whose usage patterns don't match their stated business, and turning those findings into enforced controls.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain detection logic over high‑volume API request logs and usage data in SQL and PySpark.
  • Develop behavioral baselines per client and per account, and flag deviations such as query velocity, search‑pattern shape, geographic spread, and credential reuse.
  • Investigate flagged activity end‑to‑end and write clear findings for account management and compliance.
  • Turn confirmed abuse patterns into automated rules (rate limits, blocks, and alerts), working with the API platform team.
  • Measure detection quality through false positive rates, time to detect, and coverage, and tune accordingly.
  • Maintain a library of known abuse typologies and the signals that identify each.
summary: Build and maintain detection systems for API misuse using SQL and PySpark, creating behavioral baselines and automated controls. Analyze flagged activity and improve detection quality.
